inline_prompts:
You are given a directed graph with N vertices and M edges. The vertices are numbered 1,2,\dots,N. Edge j (j=1,2,\dots,M) goes from vertex u_j to vertex v_j. It is guaranteed that vertex N is reachable from vertex 1. Initially, all edges have weight 0. We choose exactly K out of the M edges and change their weights to 1. Standard convention applies here (follow the literal input/output format given); no special handling beyond what's stated is required. Find the value of the shortest distance from vertex 1 to vertex N in the resulting graph.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N M K
u_1 v_1
u_2 v_2
\vdots
u_M v_M
Output
Print the answer.
Constraints
- 2 \leq N \leq 30
- 1 \leq K \leq M \leq 100
- 1 \leq u_j, v_j \leq N
- u_j \neq v_j
- In the given graph, vertex N is reachable from vertex 1.
- All input values are integers.
